questions.question: WXYZ is a quadrilateral in which XQ and ZP are perpendicular to WY such that XQ = ZP. Diagonals ZX and WY intersect each other at point O. If OX = 12 cm, then find the value of ZX (in cm).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When perpendiculars drawn from opposite vertices of a quadrilateral to a diagonal are equal, that diagonal bisects the other diagonal.

Therefore, diagonal WY bisects diagonal ZX at intersection point O.

This directly means OX = OZ.

Given OX = 12 cm, the full length is ZX = 2 × OX.

⇒ ZX = 2 × 12 = 24 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
• 
• 
• 
• 
 
 
• 
• W Y X Z Q P O 12 cm 

**Given:**

⇒ WXYZ is a quadrilateral with diagonal WY.

⇒ XQ ⊥ WY and ZP ⊥ WY.

⇒ XQ = ZP

⇒ OX = 12 cm

**Method Used:**

In ▵OXQ and ▵OZP:

⇒ ∠XQO = ∠ZPO = 90° (Given perpendiculars)

⇒ ∠XOQ = ∠ZOP (Vertically opposite angles are equal)

⇒ XQ = ZP (Given equal lengths)

⇒ ∴ ▵OXQ ≅ ▵OZP (By AAS congruence criterion)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since ▵OXQ ≅ ▵OZP, their corresponding parts are equal.

⇒ OX = OZ (By CPCT - Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles)

⇒ Since OX = 12 cm, we have OZ = 12 cm.

⇒ The total length of diagonal ZX = OX + OZ

⇒ ZX = 12 + 12 = 24 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

AAS Congruence Rule

If any two angles and a non-included side of one triangle are equal to the corresponding angles and side of another triangle, the two triangles are congruent.

Area of Quadrilateral Property

If perpendiculars drawn from opposite vertices to a diagonal are equal in length, the diagonal divides the entire quadrilateral into two regions of exactly equal area.

Properties of Diagonals

Whenever a diagonal line of a quadrilateral divides the other diagonal into two equal halves, it must pass strictly through the midpoint of that second diagonal.

questions.question: The area of a parallelogram with base 26 cm and height 18 cm is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The area of a parallelogram can be calculated directly by multiplying its base and the corresponding height.

Area = Base × Height

Area = 26 × 18 = 468 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 468 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Base of the parallelogram = 26 cm

Height of the parallelogram = 18 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/249e20baef5c2abf994edefade52b9a17ad0cf0109654bbdab59e0724f015953.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Area of a parallelogram = Base × Height

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = 26 × 18

⇒ Area = 468 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 468 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Parallelogram (Trigonometric)

It can also be calculated as the product of any two adjacent sides multiplied by the sine of the included angle: Area = a × b × sin(θ).

Perimeter of a Parallelogram

The perimeter is the total distance around the outside, given by the formula: 2 × (Sum of adjacent sides).

Area of a Rhombus

A rhombus is a special parallelogram with all equal sides. Its area is calculated as ½ × d₁ × d₂, where d₁ and d₂ are the lengths of the diagonals.

Area of a Trapezium

The area of a trapezium is given by ½ × (Sum of parallel sides) × Height.
</p

questions.question: R is a point outside a circle and is 18 cm away from its centre. A secant drawn from the point R intersects the circle at points A and B in such a way that RA = 7 cm and AB = 5 cm. The radius of the circle (in cm) is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to the Power of a Point theorem, for an external point at distance d from the center of a circle of radius r, the secant product is constant.

d² − r² = RA × RB

18² − r² = 7 × (7 + 5)

324 − r² = 84 ⇒ r² = 240

r = √240 = 4√15 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 4√15 cm.**

questions.question: The value of the expression sin x + cosec x = 2, then the value of sin⁷ x + cosec⁷ x is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If x + 1/x = 2, then x = 1.

Here, sin x and cosec x are reciprocals of each other.

So, sin x + 1/(sin x) = 2 ⇒ sin x = 1 and cosec x = 1.

Then, sin⁷ x + cosec⁷ x = 1⁷ + 1⁷ = 1 + 1 = 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

sin x + cosec x = 2

**Formula Used:**

cosec x = 1 / sin x

**Calculations:**

⇒ sin x + 1 / sin x = 2

⇒ (sin² x + 1) / sin x = 2

⇒ sin² x + 1 = 2 sin x

⇒ sin² x − 2 sin x + 1 = 0

⇒ (sin x − 1)² = 0

⇒ sin x = 1

Since cosec x is the reciprocal of sin x:

⇒ cosec x = 1 / 1 = 1

Now, substituting the values in the required expression:

⇒ sin⁷ x + cosec⁷ x = (1)⁷ + (1)⁷

⇒ 1 + 1 = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity of Reciprocals

If x + 1/x = 2, then x must be equal to 1. This is a standard result derived from the perfect square (x − 1)² = 0.

Negative Reciprocal Sum

If x + 1/x = −2, then x must be equal to −1. Substituting this value helps evaluate higher powers without expanding.

Trigonometric Reciprocal Pairs

The pairs (sin x, cosec x), (cos x, sec x), and (tan x, cot x) are reciprocals. If the sum of any pair is 2, the individual value of each function is exactly 1.
</p

questions.question: In a family, the combined age of husband, wife and a son is 90 years. The husband is the oldest. The difference in the ages of the husband and wife is (1)/(3)rd the age of their son. After 10 years, the age of the son would be half the age of his father. What is the present age of his mother (in years)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Son's present age be S. From the condition 10 years later, Father's present age H = 2S + 10.

From the age difference, Mother's present age W = H − S/3 = (2S + 10) − S/3 = 5S/3 + 10.

Sum of all ages is 90: (2S + 10) + (5S/3 + 10) + S = 90

⇒ 3S + 5S/3 + 20 = 90

⇒ 14S/3 = 70 ⇒ S = 15

Mother's present age = (5 × 15)/3 + 10 = 25 + 10 = 35 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 35 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Present sum of ages: H + W + S = 90

Difference between Husband and Wife: H − W = S / 3

After 10 years: S + 10 = (H + 10) / 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d971340adc37ece85070ba27b3e4c4eb7693bf613d739f31b208b10c6361d442.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ From the future age relation, 2S + 20 = H + 10

⇒ H = 2S + 10

⇒ Substituting H into the difference equation:

⇒ W = H − S / 3

⇒ W = (2S + 10) − S / 3 = (5S / 3) + 10

⇒ Substituting H and W into the sum equation:

⇒ (2S + 10) + ((5S / 3) + 10) + S = 90

⇒ 3S + 5S / 3 + 20 = 90

⇒ 14S / 3 = 70

⇒ S = 70 × 3 ÷ 14 = 15 years

⇒ The mother's present age W = (5 × 15 / 3) + 10

⇒ W = 25 + 10 = 35 years

**∴ The correct answer is 35 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Problems on Ages

If the current age is x, then the age after 'n' years will be (x + n), and the age 'n' years ago was (x − n).

Constant Age Difference

The absolute age difference between any two individuals remains constant throughout their lives, irrespective of the time period.

Ratio of Ages

When solving problems based on changing ratios over time, it is highly useful to equate the differences in their respective ratios, because the actual difference in their ages never changes.
</p

questions.question: if a + (1)/(a) = 7sqrt3 , then what is the value of a⁶ + a⁻⁶?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If x + 1/x = k, then x³ + 1/x³ = k³ − 3k

Here, a + 1/a = 7√3

⇒ a³ + 1/a³ = (7√3)³ − 3 × 7√3 = 1029√3 − 21√3 = 1008√3

Now apply the square formula (p² − 2) on the obtained result to get the 6th power:

⇒ a⁶ + a−⁶ = (1008√3)² − 2 = (1016064 × 3) − 2 = 3048192 − 2 = 3048190

**∴ The correct answer is 3048190.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a + 1/a = 7√3

**Formula Used:**

(x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy

(x + y)³ = x³ + y³ + 3xy(x + y)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Squaring both sides of the given equation:

⇒ (a + 1/a)² = (7√3)²

⇒ a² + 1/a² + 2 × a × 1/a = 147

⇒ a² + 1/a² + 2 = 147

⇒ a² + 1/a² = 145

⇒ Cubing both sides of this new equation:

⇒ (a² + 1/a²)³ = 145³

⇒ (a²)³ + (1/a²)³ + 3 × a² × (1/a²) × (a² + 1/a²) = 3048625

⇒ a⁶ + 1/a⁶ + 3 × 1 × 145 = 3048625

⇒ a⁶ + a−⁶ + 435 = 3048625

⇒ a⁶ + a−⁶ = 3048625 − 435 = 3048190

**∴ The correct answer is 3048190.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Identity Trick

If x + 1/x = k, then the value of x² + 1/x² = k² − 2.

Cube Identity Trick

If x + 1/x = k, then the value of x³ + 1/x³ = k³ − 3k.

Fifth Power Identity

If x + 1/x = k, then the value of x⁵ + 1/x⁵ = (x² + 1/x²)(x³ + 1/x³) − (x + 1/x).

Negative Power Identity

If x − 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² + 2 and x³ − 1/x³ = k³ + 3k.
</p

questions.question: What number should be subtracted from x³ - 4x² - 8x + 11 to make the number divisible by (x + 2)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the Remainder Theorem, the required number to be subtracted is simply the remainder when the polynomial is divided by (x + 2).

Substitute x = −2 directly into the given expression:

Remainder = (−2)³ − 4(−2)² − 8(−2) + 11

Remainder = −8 − 16 + 16 + 11 = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Polynomial P(x) = x³ − 4x² − 8x + 11

Divisor = (x + 2)

**Formula Used:**

For a polynomial to be exactly divisible by (x + a), the remainder P(−a) must be zero. If we subtract the remainder from the polynomial, it becomes perfectly divisible.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the number to be subtracted be k.

⇒ Modified polynomial = x³ − 4x² − 8x + 11 − k

⇒ For perfect divisibility by (x + 2), substitute x = −2 and equate to zero.

⇒ (−2)³ − 4(−2)² − 8(−2) + 11 − k = 0

⇒ −8 − 4(4) + 16 + 11 − k = 0

⇒ −8 − 16 + 16 + 11 − k = 0

⇒ −8 + 11 − k = 0

⇒ 3 − k = 0

⇒ k = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Remainder Theorem

If a polynomial P(x) is divided by a linear expression (x − a), the remainder is equal to P(a).

Factor Theorem

A polynomial P(x) has a factor (x − a) if and only if P(a) = 0. It is a specific condition of the Remainder Theorem where the remainder is zero.

Division Algorithm for Polynomials

Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder. If the remainder is subtracted from the dividend, the resulting polynomial is perfectly divisible by the divisor.
</p

questions.question: If sinA + cosA = √3, then find the value of tanA + cotA + 2sinA.cosA.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Squaring the given equation sinA + cosA = √3 yields 1 + 2sinAcosA = 3, which gives sinAcosA = 1.

The expression tanA + cotA simplifies directly to 1 / (sinAcosA).

Thus, the given expression becomes 1 / (sinAcosA) + 2sinAcosA.

Substituting sinAcosA = 1 gives 1 / 1 + 2 × 1 = 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

sinA + cosA = √3

**Formula Used:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

sin²A + cos²A = 1

tanA = sinA / cosA

cotA = cosA / sinA

**Calculations:**

⇒ Squaring both sides of the given equation:

⇒ (sinA + cosA)² = (√3)²

⇒ sin²A + cos²A + 2sinAcosA = 3

⇒ 1 + 2sinAcosA = 3

⇒ 2sinAcosA = 3 − 1

⇒ 2sinAcosA = 2

⇒ sinAcosA = 1

Now, evaluating the required expression:

⇒ tanA + cotA + 2sinAcosA

⇒ (sinA / cosA) + (cosA / sinA) + 2sinAcosA

⇒ [(sin²A + cos²A) / (sinAcosA)] + 2sinAcosA

⇒ 1 / (sinAcosA) + 2sinAcosA

Substitute the value of sinAcosA = 1 into the expression:

⇒ 1 / 1 + 2 × 1

⇒ 1 + 2 = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Trigonometric Identities

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

sec²θ − tan²θ = 1

cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1

Important Conversion

tanθ + cotθ can always be simplified directly as: (sinθ / cosθ) + (cosθ / sinθ) = (sin²θ + cos²θ) / (sinθcosθ) = 1 / (sinθcosθ).
</p

questions.question: Successive discounts of 10% and 20% are given on the purchase of a purse. If the marked price of the purse is ₹2,250, find the selling price.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive multipliers for 10% and 20% discounts are 0.9 and 0.8 respectively.

Effective Selling Price = MP × 0.9 × 0.8

SP = 2250 × 0.72

SP = 1620

**∴ The correct answer is 1620.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Marked Price (MP) = ₹2,250, First Discount (d₁) = 10%, Second Discount (d₂) = 20%

Formula Used: Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − d₁)/100 × (100 − d₂)/100

 
 MP: 2250
 
 
• 
 −10%
 
 
 2025
 
 
• 
 −20%
 
 
 SP: 1620
 
 
 
 

 
 

⇒ First discount amount = 10% of 2250 = (10/100) × 2250 = 225

⇒ Price after first discount = 2250 − 225 = 2025

⇒ Second discount amount = 20% of 2025 = (20/100) × 2025 = 405

⇒ Final Selling Price = 2025 − 405 = 1620

**∴ The correct answer is 1620.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Single Equivalent Discount

Two successive discounts of a% and b% are equal to a single discount of (a + b − ab/100)%.

Marked Price (MP)

MP is the price printed on the label of an article. Discount is always calculated on the MP.

Selling Price (SP)

SP is the final price after all discounts. SP = MP − Discount. If SP > CP, there is a profit.

questions.question: The cost of a diamond varies directly as the square of its weight. Once, this diamond broke into four pieces with weights in the ratio of 4 : 3 : 2 : 1 .When the pieces were sold, the merchant got ₹63,000 less than that of one piece. Find the original price of the diamond.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total weight = 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 parts, so Original price ∝ (10)² = 100 parts.

New total price ∝ 4² + 3² + 2² + 1² = 16 + 9 + 4 + 1 = 30 parts.

Loss in value = 100 parts − 30 parts = 70 parts.

70 parts = ₹63,000 ⇒ 1 part = ₹900.

Original price = 100 parts × ₹900 = ₹90,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹90,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Weight ratio of the four broken pieces = 4 : 3 : 2 : 1

Loss after selling the pieces = ₹63,000

**Formula Used:**

Cost (C) ∝ Weight (W)² ⇒ C = kW²

**Calculations:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a80febc336d6f24cbb76a4f6a9a5b3770abbffe68588eac7b0e95322e733a1e5.png] 

⇒ Let the weights of the broken pieces be 4x, 3x, 2x, and 1x.

⇒ Total weight of the original diamond = 4x + 3x + 2x + 1x = 10x

⇒ Original cost of the diamond = k(10x)² = 100kx²

⇒ Cost of the broken pieces = k(4x)² + k(3x)² + k(2x)² + k(x)²

⇒ Total cost of the pieces = 16kx² + 9kx² + 4kx² + 1kx² = 30kx²

⇒ Loss incurred = Original Cost − Total cost of pieces

⇒ Loss = 100kx² − 30kx² = 70kx²

⇒ Given that the loss is ₹63,000:

⇒ 70kx² = 63000

⇒ kx² = 63000 ÷ 70 = 900

⇒ Original Cost = 100kx² = 100 × 900 = 90,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹90,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportion

When a quantity varies directly as the square of another, the relation is given by y = kx². A proportional increase in x causes a quadratic increase in y.

Loss on Breakage

For any item whose value is proportional to the square of its weight, breaking it into smaller parts will strictly decrease its total value because (a + b)² > a² + b² for any positive weights.

Ratio Distribution

questions.question: The cost of tomatoes per kg is increased by 300%. A housewife reduces her consumption of tomatoes by 70%. By what percentage does her expenditure on tomatoes increase or decrease?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The net percentage change in expenditure can be found using the successive percentage formula: x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100

Here, the price increases by 300% (x = +300) and consumption decreases by 70% (y = −70).

Net change = 300 − 70 + [300 × (−70)] ÷ 100

Net change = 230 − 210 = +20%

Since the result is positive, the expenditure increases by 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is Increases, 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage increase in price = 300%

Percentage decrease in consumption = 70%

**Formula Used:**

Expenditure = Price × Consumption

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c2f710747a78f0a27df2b475103284d95ebd6ee56c73d54b8c2e0bf012f211d4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial price of tomatoes be ₹100 per kg and the initial consumption be 10 kg.

⇒ Initial Expenditure = 100 × 10 = ₹1000

⇒ New price after 300% increase = 100 + (300 ÷ 100) × 100 = ₹400 per kg

⇒ New consumption after 70% decrease = 10 − (70 ÷ 100) × 10 = 3 kg

⇒ New Expenditure = 400 × 3 = ₹1200

⇒ Change in Expenditure = 1200 − 1000 = ₹200 (Increase)

⇒ Percentage Increase = (200 ÷ 1000) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is Increases, 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a quantity is successively changed by x% and y%, the net percentage change is given by the formula: x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100. Use positive values for an increase and negative values for a decrease.

Price, Consumption, and Expenditure Relation

The foundational rule is Expenditure = Price × Consumption. If expenditure needs to remain constant while the price increases, consumption must be decreased proportionately.

Fraction Equivalent Method

For compound percentage calculations, converting percentages to fractional multipliers simplifies multiplication. For example, a 300% increase means multiplying the base value by 4, and a 70% decrease means multiplying the base value by 3/10.

questions.question: Pipe X can fill a tank in 9 hours and Pipe Y can fill it in 21 hours. If they are opened on alternate hours and Pipe X is opened first, in how many hours shall the tank be full?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity = LCM of 9 and 21 = 63 units.

Efficiency of X = 7 units/hr, Y = 3 units/hr.

Work done in 1 cycle (2 hours) = 7 + 3 = 10 units.

In 6 cycles (12 hours), work done = 60 units, remaining = 3 units.

X fills the remaining 3 units in 3/7 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 ³/₇ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Pipes are opened alternately starting with X.

⇒ Work done in 1st hour by X = 7 units

⇒ Work done in 2nd hour by Y = 3 units

⇒ Total work done in a 2-hour cycle = 7 + 3 = 10 units

⇒ In 6 cycles (12 hours), work done = 10 × 6 = 60 units

When entities work on alternate hours or days, calculate the work done in one complete cycle, multiply to get closest to the total work, and assign the remaining work to the entity whose turn is next.

questions.question: Aman invested a sum of money in scheme A at the rate of 8% p.a. for a period of 5 years on simple interest. He invested four times of the sum of scheme A in scheme B at the rate of 5% p.a. for 7 years on simple interest. He received a total interest amount of ₹1,620. How much (in ₹) did he invest in scheme B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective SI% for Scheme A = 8% × 5 = 40% of P.

Effective SI% for Scheme B = 5% × 7 = 35% of 4P = 140% of P.

Total Interest = 40% of P + 140% of P = 180% of P.

⇒ 180% of P = 1620 ⇒ P = 1620 ÷ 1.8 = 900.

Investment in Scheme B = 4P = 4 × 900 = 3600.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rate of interest for Scheme A = 8% p.a., Time = 5 years

Rate of interest for Scheme B = 5% p.a., Time = 7 years

Total interest received = ₹1,620

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6703f8dfef2fd7a47e5bce3f6e1cbbdbb2e9d465b7f547226f5a8d89398060d2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the principal amount invested in Scheme A be P.

⇒ Amount invested in Scheme B = 4P.

⇒ SI from Scheme A = (P × 8 × 5) ÷ 100 = 40P ÷ 100 = 0.4P

⇒ SI from Scheme B = (4P × 5 × 7) ÷ 100 = 140P ÷ 100 = 1.4P

⇒ Total Interest = SI from Scheme A + SI from Scheme B

⇒ Total Interest = 0.4P + 1.4P = 1.8P

⇒ 1.8P = 1620

⇒ P = 1620 ÷ 1.8 = 900

⇒ Amount invested in Scheme B = 4P = 4 × 900 = 3600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Interest Rate in SI

In Simple Interest, the effective interest rate for a given period is simply the product of the rate of interest and the time period (R × T)% of the principal.

Total Amount in Simple Interest

The total amount (A) obtained after T years is the sum of the principal (P) and the simple interest (SI). Formula: A = P + SI = P[1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In SI, the interest is calculated only on the initial principal. In Compound Interest (CI), interest is calculated on the principal and also on the accumulated interest of previous periods.

questions.question: Two trains of lengths 150 m and 250 m run on parallel lines. When they run in the same direction, they take 20 seconds to cross each other and, when they run in the opposite direction, they take 5 seconds to cross each other. What is the speed of the two trains?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance = 150 + 250 = 400 m.

Relative speed in same direction = S₁ − S₂ = 400 ÷ 20 = 20 m/s.

Relative speed in opposite direction = S₁ + S₂ = 400 ÷ 5 = 80 m/s.

Solving, S₁ = (80 + 20) ÷ 2 = 50 m/s and S₂ = (80 − 20) ÷ 2 = 30 m/s.

Speeds in km/h = 50 × (18/5) = 180 km/h and 30 × (18/5) = 108 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 180 km/h and 108 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first train (L₁) = 150 m

Length of second train (L₂) = 250 m

Time taken to cross in same direction (T₁) = 20 seconds

Time taken to cross in opposite direction (T₂) = 5 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Total distance covered to cross each other = L₁ + L₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/16430e557035d55fee350ec3e082cf14d0f49e9acdc012923f1823d994f2e282.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 150 + 250 = 400 m

⇒ Let the speed of the first train be u m/s and the second train be v m/s.

⇒ When running in the same direction, relative speed = u − v

⇒ u − v = 400 ÷ 20 = 20 m/s ... (Equation 1)

⇒ When running in opposite directions, relative speed = u + v

⇒ u + v = 400 ÷ 5 = 80 m/s ... (Equation 2)

⇒ Adding Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ 2u = 100 ⇒ u = 50 m/s

⇒ Subtracting Equation 1 from Equation 2:

⇒ 2v = 60 ⇒ v = 30 m/s

⇒ Convert speeds to km/h by multiplying with (18/5):

⇒ Speed of first train = 50 × (18/5) = 180 km/h

⇒ Speed of second train = 30 × (18/5) = 108 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 180 km/h and 108 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). When moving in the same direction, it is the difference of their speeds (|S₁ − S₂|).

Distance While Crossing

When two trains cross each other, the total distance covered is always the sum of their lengths (L₁ + L₂), regardless of the direction they are moving.

Unit Conversion Trick

To rapidly convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply the value by 18/5. To convert from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18.
</p

questions.question: ​Each of Ravi and Kavita had some marbles. Kavita had 12 more marbles than Ravi had. If each of them had one more marble, then three times the number of marbles Kavita had would be equal to four times the number of marbles Ravi had. How many marbles did Kavita actually have?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since both persons receive 1 more marble, the difference in their marble count remains 12.

The new ratio of Kavita's to Ravi's marbles is derived from 3 × Kavita = 4 × Ravi, giving a ratio of 4 : 3.

The difference in ratio parts is 4 − 3 = 1 unit.

Since 1 unit = 12 marbles, Kavita's new marble count = 4 units = 48 marbles.

Kavita's actual marbles before the addition = 48 − 1 = 47 marbles.

**∴ The correct answer is 47 marbles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Kavita had 12 more marbles than Ravi had.

If each of them gets 1 more marble, 3 × (Kavita's new marbles) = 4 × (Ravi's new marbles).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64d426fcf845436de4a00c127b3ed56339e666dd002bf08af7291306f62113bf.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Ravi's actual marbles = R

⇒ Kavita's actual marbles = R + 12

⇒ When both get 1 more marble, the difference between their totals remains 12.

⇒ 3 × (New Kavita) = 4 × (New Ravi)

⇒ (New Kavita) / (New Ravi) = 4 / 3

⇒ Difference in ratio = 4 units − 3 units = 1 unit

⇒ 1 unit corresponds to the difference of 12 marbles.

⇒ Kavita's new marbles = 4 units = 4 × 12 = 48 marbles

⇒ Kavita's actual marbles = 48 − 1 = 47 marbles

**∴ The correct answer is 47 marbles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Difference Rule

When the same uniform quantity is added to or subtracted from two numbers, the numerical difference between the two numbers remains completely unchanged.

Ratio Translation

A mathematical statement equating two products in the form "a × A = b × B" translates directly into the inverse ratio form A : B = b : a.

Direct Unitary Method

When a given quantitative value corresponds to a specific difference in ratio parts, 1 ratio unit can be calculated directly by dividing the actual difference by the ratio part difference.
</p

questions.question: 15 kg of ₹10 per kg wheat is mixed with 5 kg of another type of wheat to get a mixture costing ₹30 per kg. Find the price (per kg) of the costlier wheat.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the rule of alligation, the ratio of quantities equals the cross-difference of their unit prices.

Ratio of quantities given = 15 kg : 5 kg = 3 : 1

Using the alligation cross ratio ⇒ (x − 30) : (30 − 10) = 3 : 1

⇒ (x − 30) ÷ 20 = 3

⇒ x − 30 = 60 ⇒ x = 90

**∴ The correct answer is ₹90.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Quantity of cheaper wheat (Q₁) = 15 kg

Price of cheaper wheat (P₁) = ₹10 per kg

Quantity of costlier wheat (Q₂) = 5 kg

Average price of the mixture (Pₘ) = ₹30 per kg

Let the price of the costlier wheat be P₂ = ₹x per kg.

**Formula Used:**

Total cost of mixture = Sum of individual costs

⇒ Q₁ × P₁ + Q₂ × P₂ = (Q₁ + Q₂) × Pₘ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/04939f474ed1d2d079f8db7ced34652914bda872390bd0f3fbed45d454bc4f14.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ 15 × 10 + 5 × x = (15 + 5) × 30

⇒ 150 + 5x = 20 × 30

⇒ 150 + 5x = 600

⇒ 5x = 600 − 150

⇒ 5x = 450

⇒ x = 90

**∴ The correct answer is ₹90.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rule of Alligation

It gives the exact ratio in which two ingredients at different prices must be mixed to obtain a desired average mixture price. Formula: Q꜀ₕₑₐₚₑᵣ ÷ Q꜀ₒₛₜₗᵢₑᵣ = (P꜀ₒₛₜₗᵢₑᵣ − Pₘₑₐₙ) ÷ (Pₘₑₐₙ − P꜀ₕₑₐₚₑᵣ).

Weighted Average Method

The rule of alligation is practically a simplified cross-multiplication of the weighted average formula Pₘ = (Q₁P₁ + Q₂P₂) ÷ (Q₁ + Q₂).

Versatility of Alligation

The Alligation shortcut is not only restricted to price and mixture amounts; it is universally applicable across chapters like Speed & Distance, Percentages, Profit & Loss, and Averages.

questions.question: If 3sin²θ + 5cos²θ = 4 and θ is an acute angle, then the value of tanθ is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Divide the entire equation by cos²θ to get: 3tan²θ + 5 = 4sec²θ

Substitute sec²θ = 1 + tan²θ into the equation:

3tan²θ + 5 = 4(1 + tan²θ)

5 − 4 = 4tan²θ − 3tan²θ ⇒ tan²θ = 1

Since θ is an acute angle, tanθ = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

3sin²θ + 5cos²θ = 4

**Formula Used:**

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

tanθ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

**Calculations:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6cc54a0066dd9758470ddc86e9968dbd107cf381a459c238687a3ea758b455d9.png] 

⇒ 3sin²θ + 3cos²θ + 2cos²θ = 4

⇒ 3(sin²θ + cos²θ) + 2cos²θ = 4

⇒ 3(1) + 2cos²θ = 4

⇒ 2cos²θ = 1

⇒ cos²θ = 1 / 2

⇒ cosθ = 1 / √2

⇒ Since θ is an acute angle, θ = 45°

⇒ tanθ = tan(45°) = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.

Angles in the First Quadrant

For any acute angle (0° < θ < 90°), all six trigonometric ratios (sin, cos, tan, cot, sec, cosec) are positive.

Values at 45°

When θ = 45°, the perpendicular and base of a right triangle are equal in length, giving tan(45°) = 1 and sin(45°) = cos(45°) = 1/√2.
